Ambient restoration is inside the factory and precedes later CreateActivity evaluation.

The nonnullable Lazy factory does not catch the construction failure, so the required source remains required and the selected original exception is cached by the value factory rather than wrapped by an eager class initializer. Existing argument checks and required initial timestamp remain outside the observational isolation. Listener registration and activation remain inside constructor ownership unwind. The factory restores the captured live ambient activity before CreateActivity can capture its parent; the outer activation finally independently restores the instance caller context.

Only the constructor catch around already-failed activation suppresses a secondary Dispose exception. Bare throw preserves the primary exception object/stack after the nested cleanup. Dispose itself still marks the instance disposed, clears observations, completes waiters, stops the activity using the existing guard, then attempts listener and timer disposal in nested finally blocks. Ordinary standalone Dispose and the public caller using-scope still propagate required timer-cleanup errors.

Public DI telemetry registration resolves the listener in ContainerTestHarness construction; public publish/send/request extensions and ActAsync create TrackedActivity and own normal cleanup. No production clock, action, cancellation, timer schedule, idle deadline, request result or business operation was moved into a new optional catch.
